title: Foreign ownership limit on Qantas
summary: The Qantas Sale Act 1992 requires Qantas's constitution to keep foreign persons' interests to no more than 49% of its issued share capital.
direction_rationale: A statutory cap on foreign ownership of one firm limits who can own and finance it.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no dates. The 25% and 35% limits the Act once set are no longer in its text.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 17 November 2026 (phase 6 of the levers re-evaluation, batch 1) from the law quoted. Not yet checked: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Caps foreign ownership of Qantas at 49%, written into its constitution by law. It narrows the pool of capital and owners for one airline; other airlines face no such cap under this Act.

marks.reason: Shuts foreign investors out of majority ownership of one major airline.

assessment.confidence_note: The cap is explicit; its effect on Qantas's cost of capital has not been measured.

responsible.note: The department responsible for aviation; not checked against the administrative arrangements order.
